nyc.name: NYC film permits
nyc.about: 33,502 film permits issued by New York City (2011–2018): event type, start and end date/time, borough, community boards, category and zip code. Comma-separated with quoted text fields.

etl1.name: Balance sheet extract (messy)
etl1.about: Balance sheet data for several companies (2016–2018). Contains duplicates, unquoted commas, K/M suffixes, numbers in parentheses and inconsistent units.

etl2.name: Employee codes
etl2.about: 597 employees. EmployeeCode combines Location (3 letters), EmpID (4 digits), PlantID (after the hyphen) and PayPeriod (W/M), e.g. JAP1080-19M.

etl3.name: Employee codes (messy)
etl3.about: Same idea as Case 2 but messier: location codes of different lengths (US, ARG, Japan), 1–3 digit EmpIDs, 1–2 digit PlantIDs and pay periods recorded as W, M or Mo.

etl4.name: Hotel journal entries
etl4.about: 789 journal-entry lines for a hotel and conference center with lookup tabs: BusinessUnits, ChartOfAccounts, PreparerInfo (PreparerID unique only within a business unit) and Source.

integrateco.name: IntegrateCo payroll
integrateco.about: Pipe-delimited (|) .csv files: 2015 payroll (one row per employee, job and pay date), 2016 payroll from a new system (no dates, Gross_Wages combined), job codes (001–012, stored as text) and employee locations.

chinook.name: Chinook music store
chinook.about: A digital music store: Customer, Invoice, InvoiceLine, Track, Album, Artist, Genre, Employee, MediaType and Playlist tables.

songs.name: Spotify top songs
songs.about: Tables songs (name, artist_id, danceability, energy, valence, tempo, duration_ms, …) and artists (id, name).

movies.name: IMDb movies · practice subset
movies.about: Movies with at least 5,000 IMDb votes. Tables movies, people, stars, directors and ratings. Answers on this site are computed on this subset.

fiftyville.name: Fiftyville mystery
fiftyville.about: Town records: crime_scene_reports, interviews, courthouse_security_logs, atm_transactions, bank_accounts, phone_calls, flights, airports, passengers, people.

pcards.name: OSU purchasing cards · 2014
pcards.about: All 116,031 Oklahoma State University P-card transactions in calendar year 2014 (table pcards). Negative amounts are returns. TransactionDate is stored as text (M/D/YYYY).

questions.prompt: The warehouse controller wants a simpler model and asks you to remove one variable. Based on the regression output, which one would you remove — or would you keep them all? Why?
questions.answer: None — every predictor has a p-value below 0.05, so each one adds explanatory power. Dropping one would make the model simpler but worse. Statistical significance only says an effect is unlikely to be zero; whether it matters for the business depends on its size.

keypoints.label: Used the p-values / 5% level
keypoints.probe: What in the regression output are you basing that on?

keypoints.label: Chose to keep all variables
keypoints.probe: Is there any variable you would remove, and why or why not?

keypoints.label: Explained what a high/low p-value means
keypoints.probe: What does a p-value above 0.05 actually tell you about that variable?

keypoints.label: Answered the follow-up (see what the examiner listens for)

followup.ask: Does 'statistically significant' mean the effect is important for the business?
followup.listen: No — significance says the effect is unlikely to be zero; importance depends on its size in context.

questions.prompt: A colleague used the model to predict count differences for counts done on paper with 8,000 stock items counted and got 76.6 items with a difference. Should the warehouse controller rely on this number?
questions.answer: No, not without a strong warning. The model was estimated on data with items counted from 200 to 4,000 items, so 8,000 stock items counted lies outside the observed range. This is extrapolation: the linear relationship may not hold there. Use values inside the range, or collect data that covers this situation.

keypoints.label: Said the value is outside the observed range
keypoints.probe: What range of values was the model actually estimated on?

keypoints.label: Called it extrapolation / unreliable
keypoints.probe: What is the risk of using the model for a value like that?

keypoints.label: Mentioned the observed range (200–4,000)
keypoints.probe: Can you tell me the range the data covers?

keypoints.label: Answered the follow-up (see what the examiner listens for)

followup.ask: So what would you tell the warehouse controller instead of just giving that number?
followup.listen: Warn that it is outside the data; offer a prediction within the range, or suggest collecting more data.
